extracted.intended_audience: researchers, funders, and grant administrators studying peer review and grant-selection processes
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating cardiovascular research grant-in-aid applications using a three-tier peer-review system (internal reviewers, external reviewers, and committee discussion), and identifying predictors of scientific-merit scores and sources of inter-reviewer variance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific merit
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall evaluation of the quality of the proposed research (the primary 'scientific-merit' score used by HSFO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the main outcome scored by internal reviewers, external reviewers, and the committee; committee discussion shifted scientific-merit scores in ways not predictable from individual reviewer scores alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant qualifications and track record
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the applicant's qualifications, career stage, and prior funding history as indicators of ability to carry out the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captured as an applicant characteristic in the study and treated as a predictor of scientific-merit scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology and feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the soundness of methods, study design, and practicality/feasibility of completing the project as proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed among HSFO's implicit criteria and tested as a variable influencing reviewers' scientific-merit scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance to cardiovascular science and clinical care
rubrics_metrics.description: Judge the importance and potential impact of the proposed research for cardiovascular science or clinical practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in HSFO criteria as a distinct dimension affecting final score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonableness of budget request
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether the requested budget is appropriate and justified for the proposed scope of work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recorded as an application characteristic (requested budget) and explicitly listed among implicit HSFO review criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional environment and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of the applicant's institution, available resources, and whether the environment supports successful completion of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included both as an implicit HSFO criterion and as an applicant characteristic ('institution') tested in the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of research (basic, clinical, applied)
rubrics_metrics.description: Categorization of the proposal by research type (basic, clinical, applied), which may influence reviewers' assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captured as an application characteristic and analyzed as a predictor of scientific-merit scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The specific scientific discipline or subfield of the proposal, recorded as an application characteristic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included among variables tested for association with reviewers' scores; discipline may shape perceived relevance and expertise matching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant's career stage (e.g., junior vs senior), considered as part of applicant characteristics that can affect scoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treated as a predictor variable in the study; may interact with expectations about productivity and feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior funding history
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant's history of previous grants or funding successes, used as a signal of capability and track record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recorded and analyzed as an applicant characteristic predicting scientific-merit scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer role: internal vs external
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a reviewer is an internal committee scientist or an externally solicited expert; reviewer role as a determinant of scoring and influence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key finding: internal and external reviewers showed substantial disagreement; final committee scores were better predicted by internal reviewers than external reviewers, implying committees privilege in-group judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer geographic location
rubrics_metrics.description: Geographic location of reviewers (e.g., local vs distant) treated as a reviewer characteristic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captured in the study as a potential predictor of scoring differences between reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer prior committee service
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether reviewers have prior experience serving on the committee, recorded as a reviewer attribute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included among reviewer characteristics tested as predictors of scoring patterns and agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of reviewers per application
rubrics_metrics.description: The count of reviewers assigned to an application (internal + external), treated as a process characteristic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recorded and analyzed; number of reviewers contributes to variance in scores and to the information/variance trade-off inherent in multi-tier review architectures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter-reviewer agreement (level of agreement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree of concordance among reviewers' scientific-merit scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Found to be modest in this dataset, consistent with broader peer-review literature; modest agreement implies limited reliability of single-reviewer judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing in committee meeting
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application is discussed during the committee meeting (a process/timing variable potentially affecting outcomes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captured as a process characteristic; timing can influence discussion dynamics and final scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee discussion and final scoring dynamics
rubrics_metrics.description: How committee deliberation alters individual reviewer scores to produce a final committee score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study found committee discussion shifted scores unpredictably from individual reviewer scores; committee deliberation introduces additional variance and can privilege internal perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative weight/influence of internal reviewers in final decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which internal reviewer assessments predict or determine the committee's final scores compared with external reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical finding: final committee scores were better predicted by internal reviewers than by external reviewers, suggesting the committee structure confers greater influence to in-group/internal reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-tier review architecture effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition that having multiple review tiers (internal, external, committee) introduces sources of variance beyond simply aggregating more information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implication for rubric design: multi-tier architectures can change outcome distributions and reliability characteristics; external reviews may be primarily advisory rather than determinative in such systems.
